title: Microsoft Purview: DLP inline protection for more unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout targets, licensing, prerequisites and documented controls are supported. Narrow the unsupported statement that security groups are read-only, finish the UI route to browser enforcement, and reconcile checklist items missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Purview collection and DLP policies will support inline browser protection for a significantly broader set of unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention (DLP) policies will support browser inline protection for a significantly broader set of unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Admins can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data shared through supported browser activities.
claims.quote: Admins can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data shared through supported browser activities, helping extend consistent data security controls across more destinations.

claims.claim: Edge for Business enforces Purview DLP policies inline.
claims.quote: With a DLP policy, admins can apply inline data protection to identify, audit, and protect sensitive data in interactions with cloud apps (unmanaged and managed) in Microsoft Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps in the browser apply to Edge for Business on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices.
claims.quote: DLP policies that target unmanaged apps in the browser apply to Microsoft Edge for Business on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices managed by Microsoft Intune.

claims.claim: Devices covered by the unmanaged-app browser policies are managed by Microsoft Intune.
claims.quote: You can use policies for unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business on Intune-managed devices and the policies apply across all Edge browser profiles (work profile, personal profile and InPrivate).

claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps on managed devices apply across all Edge browser profiles.
claims.quote: Policies targeting unmanaged apps on managed devices apply across all Edge browser profiles (work profile, personal profile and InPrivate).

claims.claim: The currently documented supported unmanaged apps include ChatGPT (consumer).
claims.quote:
Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps:
- Adobe Firefly
- CapCut
- ChatGPT (consumer)

claims.claim: The currently documented supported unmanaged apps include Google Gemini.

- DeepSeek

claims.claim: Learn does not yet identify the expanded app set for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: '"571396" "Edge" unmanaged apps' and 'Purview expanded inline protection unmanaged apps Edge 571396 licensing pricing default January 2027'; read dlp-browser-dlp-learn and dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge. They list current apps, not this expansion's additions.

claims.claim: The displayed Purview path reaches the unmanaged AI app scope and the browser enforcement selection.
claims.quote:
Select + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes
Select All unmanaged AI apps > Add.
On the Choose where to enforce the policy step, select Edge for Business.
claims.fix: The printed steps correctly reach app selection but stop before enforcement selection. Extend the path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Choose where to enforce the policy > Edge for Business'. User/group selection and wizard navigation can remain omitted.

claims.claim: Adaptive app scopes apply only to supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Not all unmanaged AI apps are supported in Edge for Business. Adaptive app scopes apply only to the supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Saving the first collection or DLP policy targeting unmanaged apps in Edge triggers automatic configuration by the Microsoft Edge management service.
claims.quote: After you save your first Purview collection or DLP policy targeting unmanaged apps in Edge for Business, the Microsoft Edge management service automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies, Microsoft Intune policies, and security groups

claims.claim: Activation automatically creates Edge configuration policies outside Purview.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Edge management service creates Edge configuration policies that activate in-browser policies in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Activation automatically creates Microsoft Intune policies outside Purview.
claims.quote: Microsoft Intune policies are created automatically to help prevent circumvention outside of Edge.

claims.claim: Activation automatically creates security groups outside Purview.
claims.quote: Security groups are created and updated automatically.

claims.where: What's changing; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A DLP policy configured to block prevents in-scope users from using unprotected browsers where the policy does not apply.
claims.quote: If you configure the DLP policy to block, users in scope can't use unprotected browsers where the policy doesn't apply.

claims.claim: Apps missing from the supported-app list are not covered by this browser inline control.
claims.quote: Not all unmanaged AI apps are supported in Edge for Business. Adaptive app scopes apply only to the supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how this expansion changes existing policies scoped to all unmanaged AI apps.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview browser DLP adaptive app scopes newly added apps automatically existing policies unmanaged AI apps'; read the roadmap, browser DLP overview, creation walkthrough and Edge activation page. None states this expansion's effect on existing policies.

claims.claim: Detection uses destination-app traffic, which is not always exactly the same as the originating app.
claims.quote: When you target an unmanaged cloud app in an Edge for Business browser policy, detection is based on the destination app's traffic, which isn't always exactly the same as the originating app.

claims.claim: Apps such as ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI may intermittently use encoded content or dynamic endpoints, affecting enforcement.
claims.quote: Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers up to 4 MB of content for uploadText.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview browser and network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview browser and network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: An unmanaged-app policy can capture consumer and enterprise interactions where the URL is shared, including ChatGPT consumer and enterprise.
claims.quote: Policies that target unmanaged apps can capture interactions from both the consumer and enterprise versions of an app when the app's URL is shared across instances (for example, ChatGPT consumer and ChatGPT enterprise).

claims.claim: Activation creates two security groups.
claims.quote: 2 security groups are created — one for included users and one for excluded users — that match the scope of your Purview policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: The automatically created Edge configuration and Intune policies are read-only.
claims.quote: Automatically created policies are read-only and are updated automatically by making updates to the policies in Purview.

claims.claim: The automatically created security groups are read-only.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview automatically created security groups read only Edge DLP'; read microsoft-edge-dlp-purview-configuration, including How it works and FAQs. Microsoft calls policies read-only and groups automatically managed, but does not state that groups are read-only.
claims.fix: Replace 'the auto-created Edge configuration policies, Intune policies and security groups are read-only and are updated by editing the Purview policy' with 'the auto-created Edge configuration policies and Intune policies are read-only; these policies and the security groups update automatically when the Purview policy changes'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changes made to Purview policies automatically update the associated policies and groups outside Purview.
claims.quote: Once initially created, these policies and groups stay in sync and update automatically when changes are made to the Purview policies and don’t require extra setup or ongoing management by administrators outside of Purview.

claims.claim: Users included in blocking policies are blocked from using Firefox and other browsers.
claims.quote: In Firefox and other browsers: Use of these browsers is blocked.

claims.claim: Chrome use might be allowed for users in blocking-policy scope.
claims.quote: In Chrome browser: Use of the browser might be allowed depending on policy scope.

claims.claim: When Chrome use is allowed, access to a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps is blocked.
claims.quote: If allowed, access to a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps is blocked.

claims.quote: If automatic behaviors fail to create or update the policies or groups, an error message displays in Purview and policies aren't applied in Edge for Business.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
